summary: Describes the de facto Digest Message Format, a way of bundling many mail messages into one message, as used by mailing lists. It is an elective experimental protocol.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 1153 describes how to put several mailing-list messages inside one email. It defines markers and header rules so software can separate the messages again.

questions: what is a mailing list digest
how are messages separated in a digest
which headers are kept in a digest
subtitle: A format for combining mailing-list messages into a single digest.

tldr.problem: Busy mailing lists need a way to distribute several messages together while preserving enough structure to separate them later.
tldr.mechanism: A digest is one conventional email containing a preamble, one or more enclosed messages separated by lines of 30 hyphens, and a two-line trailer.
tldr.outcome: RFC 1153 documents a de facto digest format and says it does not replace the generic encapsulation format in RFC 934.

today: RFC 1153 is an Experimental memo describing a de facto Digest Message Format. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why Digests Were Used
sections.content: Moderators of high-traffic mailing lists developed a digest format to combine several messages into one composite message for redistribution. The RFC says this reduces mailer load and conserves network bandwidth by reducing repeated message-header information. It documents the format so programs can create and separate digests compatibly.
sections.plainLanguage: A digest groups several list messages into one email. The format helps software split them back into separate messages.

sections.title: Parts of a Digest
sections.content: The digest body contains a preamble, one or more enclosed messages, and a trailer. The preamble usually has a table of contents and is separated from the messages by a line of 70 hyphens and a blank line. Each enclosed message has a header and body; messages are separated by blank lines and a line of 30 hyphens.
sections.plainLanguage: The digest starts with an introduction, then contains the original messages, and ends with a trailer. Lines of hyphens mark the boundaries.

sections.title: Preserving Message Details
sections.content: When rebuilding an enclosed message's header, the format retains Date, From, To, Cc, Subject, Message-ID, and Keywords when present, in that order. Retaining Summary is optional; other header lines should be discarded, especially Received lines. The trailer's first line begins with “End of” and the list name, followed by Digest; the second line is a row of asterisks.
sections.plainLanguage: The format keeps key header fields in a set order and removes other headers. Its final lines identify the end of the digest.
